preview.author: Sridhar Bhamidi

pick.text: Going by the recent results of these two sides, both teams to score and over 2.5 goals look like a distinct possibility for this match.

preview.synopsis: Glimt are strong at home and chasing a knockout place. Writer picks both teams to score and over 2.5 goals (no outcome covered).

strengths.home: Three wins in four, 4-2 at Molde; won ten of last 12 competitive home games; W1 D1 L2 in the league phase; no new injury worries.
strengths.away: Andres Andrade injured in last match; first Austrian opponent for Glimt in this phase is a third meeting with Austrian sides.

preview.author: Matthew Billon

pick.text: A Galatasaray win makes great appeal at the prices based on their superior form and imperious home record this term.

preview.synopsis: First-ever meeting. Galatasaray hold the form and home record edge. Writer backs a Galatasaray win.

strengths.home: Six straight league wins, two-goal wins in last two UCL games; only Barcelona have beaten them at home this season; Osimhen on the injury list.
strengths.away: Poor recent run after six wins; Matty Cash out; English sides failed to win nine of ten visits to Galatasaray.

fixtures.competition: AFC Champions League Elite League Phase

preview.synopsis: Wrexham arrive in steadier form; last meeting was a 2-2 draw. AI stats preview, no writer's pick.

strengths.home: 18th on 18 points (16-26), lost 0-2 at Middlesbrough, one win in last five; Smith out, O'Hare and Windass doubts.
strengths.away: 14th on 21 points (19-20), won 1-0 at Lincoln, three unbeaten.

preview.synopsis: Cardiff have the home and attacking edge over the bottom club; Preston have won one of the last five meetings. AI stats preview, no writer's pick.

strengths.home: 15th on 18 points (28-29), lost 2-1 to Norwich; unbeaten in eight home games; xG 1.94 per match; Osho out, Ng doubt.
strengths.away: 24th on 9 points (14-31), 1-1 with West Ham; winless in eight; Kenny, Clarke and Gibson out.

preview.synopsis: Relegation-zone clash between struggling sides; the last meeting was a 2-2 draw. AI stats preview, no writer's pick.

strengths.home: 19th on 17 points (14-25), lost 1-2 at Wolves, one win in five; worst xG in the league; Ramsay and Chalobah doubts.
strengths.away: 20th on 15 points (15-27), lost 0-1 to Wrexham, one win in five; Darikwa out.

preview.synopsis: Leaders at home against a side that has lost three straight away; last meeting was a 2-2 draw. AI stats preview, no writer's pick.

strengths.home: Lead the Championship on 32 points (32-19), beat Bristol City 2-0; unbeaten in eight at home; best shot volume; Jones, Tymon and Ronald out.
strengths.away: Eighth on 27 points (24-20), 2-2 with West Brom; lost last three away.

preview.synopsis: Norwich's five-match winning run meets a well-placed QPR; recent meetings average 3.2 goals. AI stats preview, no writer's pick.

strengths.home: 11th on 24 points (34-25), five straight wins scoring 3.4 per game; Toure and Diallo out.
strengths.away: Seventh on 27 points (25-18), won 1-0 at Millwall, unbeaten in three; Lloyd doubt, Mbengue out.

preview.synopsis: West Ham have the stronger attack but are winless in five; Portsmouth lost four of the last five meetings. AI stats preview, no writer's pick.

strengths.home: 12th on 23 points (21-19), 1-1 at Bolton, two wins in five; Bishop and Arthur out, Milovanovic doubt.
strengths.away: 10th on 24 points (38-24), 1-1 with Preston, five without a win; Walker-Peters out.

preview.synopsis: Southampton carry a strong head-to-head record and the better goal difference. AI stats preview, no writer's pick.

strengths.home: Ninth on 25 points (25-19), beat Watford 4-0; four home games unbeaten; Tanganga suspended, Seriki and Rothwell out.
strengths.away: Sixth on 27 points (31-15), beat Derby 2-0; won last six meetings with Sheffield United; xG 1.87.

preview.synopsis: Leicester are better placed on form and shots conceded; recent meetings average 3.0 goals. AI stats preview, no writer's pick.

strengths.home: 22nd on 12 points (18-24), lost 2-1 to Wigan, one win in five; worst xGA in the league; Honeyman and Earl out.
strengths.away: 10th on 22 points (23-19), won 1-0 at Huddersfield, three wins in five; McFarlane and Stolarczyk out.

preview.synopsis: Bradford are strong defensively against the bottom side that has gone ten without a win. AI stats preview, no writer's pick.

strengths.home: Sixth on 23 points (12-10), 2-2 with Doncaster, one win in five; best shots-on-target conceded; Pointon out, Lapslie doubt.
strengths.away: 24th on 9 points (14-26), lost 1-2 at Sheffield Wednesday; ten without a win.

preview.synopsis: First-ever meeting. Wycombe lose two suspended defenders; Bromley are in the bottom three. AI stats preview, no writer's pick.

strengths.home: 23rd on 12 points (14-33), won 1-0 at Reading; xG 0.94; fewest touches in the opposition box.
strengths.away: 15th on 18 points (24-27), lost 4-3 at Oxford; Casey and Leahy suspended after red cards.

preview.synopsis: Sheffield Wednesday are better placed; Stevenage won both recent meetings. AI stats preview, no writer's pick.

strengths.home: 14th on 19 points, won 1-0 at Notts County; good headed-goal and xGA numbers; Kemp and Roberts doubts, Burstow and James out.
strengths.away: Fifth on 26 points, won 2-1 at Barnsley, four unbeaten; best big-chance creation.

fixtures.competition: Northern Ireland League Cup Second Round
Northern Ireland League Cup Second Round

preview.synopsis: Hibernian won four of the last five meetings, including 2-1 earlier this season; Dundee arrive after an 0-8 defeat. AI stats preview, no writer's pick.

strengths.home: 11th on 11 points (15-21), lost 0-4 to Dundee United, one win in five; Lowe and Megwa out.
strengths.away: Seventh on 17 points (18-23), lost 0-8 to Hearts; Bevan suspended, Moorhouse out.

preview.synopsis: Wolves are well ahead on form and attack; they won three of the last five meetings. AI stats preview, no writer's pick.

strengths.home: Third on 31 points (28-19), beat Charlton 2-1, four wins in last five at home; xG 1.83.
strengths.away: 23rd on 10 points (14-32), lost 2-0 at Southampton; winless in six away; Szmodics out, Hedges doubt.

preview.author: Ryan Fisher

pick.text: Arsenal are a different proposition without Raya, which makes both teams to score a much more attractive option here.

preview.synopsis: Arsenal are strong at the Emirates but lose their goalkeeper. Writer picks both teams to score (no outcome covered).

strengths.home: Unbeaten start (W3 D1), 2-2 with Newcastle; won 15 of last 16 league phase games; Raya and Zubimendi likely out.
strengths.away: Lost three of four UCL trips to Arsenal; Guirassy and Chukwuemeka missed the weekend.

preview.author: Tomáš Vlasák

pick.text: With Como in sparkling form this campaign, a wager on Como to triumph by two or more goals carries strong appeal.

preview.synopsis: First competitive meeting. Como are in sparkling form with 19 UCL goals. Writer backs Como to win by two or more goals.

strengths.home: Nine points from four UCL rounds after a 9-1 win over Lens; seven wins in last eight; unbeaten at home.
strengths.away: Unbeaten in last five against Italian sides; Arriaga hurt, Koita suspended.

preview.author: Aaron Murphy

pick.text: With Feyenoord’s slump and FC Porto’ winning streak in mind, backing FC Porto to win seems the obvious choice.

preview.synopsis: Feyenoord are in a slump and leak goals in the UCL. Writer backs Porto to win.

strengths.home: A point off the top 24; lost nine of last 12 European games; six without a win, lost at home to Excelsior; Hadj Moussa doubt.
strengths.away: Winning streak; William Gomes doubtful.

preview.author: Chris Wilson

pick.text: Neither side boasts particularly sparkling form, but Napoli’s recent record on the road in this competition (scoring in six of their eight-game winless streak) is enough to suggest there’s value in a Manchester City win and both teams to score.

preview.synopsis: City have won the last three meetings. Writer sees value on Napoli, whose pick does not name a clear outcome.

strengths.home: Three wins from four in the league phase, no win inside 90 minutes in last five domestic games; lost two of last 27 home UCL matches; De Bruyne back against his old club.
strengths.away: Eleven matches without a win; lengthy injury list; scoring in six of the eight.

preview.author: Tomáš Vlasák

pick.text: With RB Leipzig firing on all cylinders and Lens in disarray, a punt on RB Leipzig to score 3+ goals holds plenty of appeal.

preview.synopsis: First-ever meeting. Leipzig are firing at home. Writer backs Leipzig to score 3+ goals.

strengths.home: Lost three of four in the UCL but won four straight in the Bundesliga after a 5-1 win; won six of seven home games; Ouedraogo out until the new year.
strengths.away: In disarray by the writer's account; Ivanovic hoped back.

preview.author: John Pennington

pick.text: With Real Madrid’s UCL matches producing an average of five goals per game this term, backing over 4.5 goals could be a bold option worth pursuing.

preview.synopsis: First meeting since 1988/89; Madrid's UCL games average five goals. Writer picks over 4.5 goals (no outcome covered).

strengths.home: Nine straight wins in all competitions, won 2-1 against Celta; won all eight home games this season; conceded seven in four UCL wins; no new injuries.
strengths.away: Eredivisie leaders; Mauro Junior doubt after being substituted.

preview.author: Ben Olawumi

pick.text: Given how one-sided this game is widely expected to be and how badly Slovan Bratislava have fared in Europe this term, Betis to win both halves looks very viable.

preview.synopsis: Never met before and the widest gap in the phase. Writer backs Betis to win both halves.

strengths.home: Bottom of the table, lost all four league phase games each by 3+ goals; lost all 12 UCL matches; Cerepkai and Camara out.
strengths.away: Competing at the top end; Antony hurt, Ceballos a major doubt.
